title: latency-suspect-hunt-workflow-drafts
body:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic workflow + interaction sketch for a "latency suspect hunt" experience in the Console trace viewer. Goal: help engineers go from alert -> root-suspect in under 3 minutes for common classes of latency regressions (cold start, KV cache misses, backend stall, tokenization spike, network tail).

Context / audience:
- Product: Console trace/trace-list owner (me)
- Primary users: platform engineers, SREs, product engineers on customer accounts
- Secondary: solutions engineers doing postmortems, support reps triaging customer tickets

High-level flow (user story):
1) Alert triggers (latency anomaly on route X). User opens trace list filtered to route X and time window.
2) Select a high-latency trace -> open trace viewer in 'investigate' mode (persistent left rail).
3) Quick fingerprint: show top 3 suspects (KV miss, model fallback, long IO) derived from heuristics/metadata.
4) Drill into suspect span: pin span, view nearby sibling spans, compare distribution across 20-sample traces.
5) Confirm suspect or mark as inconclusive -> run automated rerun test / attach to ticket.

Key UX components (sketch descriptions):
- Investigator rail (left): compact summary + controls
  - fingerprint row: 3 suspect chips with confidence % (hover to see why)
  - quick actions: "pin suspect", "open side-by-side", "run synthetic"
  - trace metadata: model id, model variant, infra tier, region, cold-start flag

- Waterfall centerpane (main):
  - continuous timeline with virtualization (supports 10k spans)
  - suspect marker lane above waterfall: colored bands (red/orange/yellow) mapped to suspect reasons
  - span row affordances: hover-to-preview payload, right-click to open details flyout, double-click to zoom-in on parent
  - timeline scrubber: small histogram + selectable window for focusing (5s / 30s / full)

- Right flyout (ephemeral):
  - span details, logs, annotations, raw headers, KV cache hit/miss tag
  - quick compare: show average latency for the same span across selected sample traces

- Sample trace carousel (bottom):
  - horizontal strip of thumbnails (time-scaled mini-waterfalls) for 20 sampled traces from the same query group
  - select multiple thumbnails to enable "diff" mode (side-by-side waterfalls)

Interaction patterns & microcopy notes:
- Suspect chips: concise labels ("KV cache miss", "Model fallback", "Network tail") with confidence and brief rationale on hover (e.g., "high number of downstream 500s + increased connection wait time").
- Pinning: pin remains sticky across traces in current investigation tab. Pinned spans show a small badge and can be included in bookmarks/export.
- Keyboard shortcuts (draft):
  - K/J: move selection up/down spans
  - P: pin current span
  - D: open diff mode (requires at least 2 selected traces)
  - F: open filter quickbar (see grammar below)
- Filter quickbar grammar (examples to support fast hunting):
  - status:500..599 -> show server errors
  - tag:kv_hit=false -> show cache misses
  - service:embedder and duration:>200ms -> narrow to embedding service slow spans
  - path:/api/generate and model:"redwood-mini-7b" -> route + model intersection
  - combined example: status:500 tag:db_connections>50 within:5m

Heuristics and fingerprinting (implementation notes):
- Compute suspect reasons from a small rule set plus lightweight ML ranking (fast):
  - rules: cache miss present, model fallback used, downstream 5xx spikes, long DNS/connect times, large request payloads
  - features for ranker: span duration percentile, sibling span skew, new-model-version-flag, infra host churn, KV miss rate
- Show top-3 suspects and allow user to expand rationale (trace examples that triggered the rule)

Edge cases and constraints:
- Very large traces (>50k spans): ensure virtualization + sampling. Investigator rail must not block rendering. Show a fidelity indicator (sampled vs full).
- Multi-region traces: timeline should show region swimlanes or region annotation on spans.
- Missing instrumentation: provide a "what's missing" CTA (e.g., "no KV tags found — install sdk v1.4+")

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Investigator rail exists, shows fingerprint chips with hover rationale
- Pinning of spans works and persists in current tab
- Sample trace carousel populated with 20 sampled traces and supports selection for diff
- Filter quickbar supports basic grammar (status, tag, service, duration, path, model) and updates waterfall in real-time
- Diff mode shows two traces side-by-side with synchronized scrubber and highlighted suspect spans

Backlog tickets (draft scope):
- PROJ-49: investigator-rail UI + API for fingerprints
- PROJ-50: pinning mechanic + persistence
- PROJ-51: sample-carousel + server sampling endpoint
- PROJ-52: filter-grammar parser + quickbar UX
- PROJ-53: diff mode rendering + synchronized scrubbing

Open questions / discussion items:
- How to compute confidence scores cheaply at query time? (approx ranker vs batch precompute)
- Should suspect chips be clickable to auto-filter other traces with same suspect pattern? (pro: speed; con: surprising filter changes)
- Export format for pinned spans: JSON vs CSV vs trace-link bundle?
- Privacy: when surfacing "rationale" examples, are we comfortable showing snippet of logs/headers in RBAC-limited accounts?

Quick sketches (verbal):
- Investigator rail top -> fingerprint chips -> below: metadata rows -> actions row (pin, diff, synthetic)
- Waterfall center -> suspect lane above -> waterfall rows with per-span small colored left border for severity
- Bottom carousel -> thumbnails that expand on hover to 3x height

To-dos before grooming: 
- Product: pick prioritization order for PROJ-49..53
- Eng: prototype cheap suspect ranker (fast rules engine)
- Design: produce 2 visual comps for investor rail + diff mode (desktop + narrow laptop widths)
- SRE: validate performance on 50k-span traces using trace-synth tool

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally lightweight and focused on the investigator flow (not full trace-editing or annotations). Look for missing quick actions you'd expect when you're "hunting" a latency spike (e.g., run-synthetic, schedule-replay, open-flamegraph).
